subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should all Origin-bearing gateway-authenticated plugin HTTP requests be required to pass the Control UI origin policy, including explicit auth.mode="none" private-ingress deployments?
rationale: The repository documents origin enforcement for trusted-proxy browser requests, but the permanent policy for explicit no-auth private ingress affects both browser security and supported non-browser automation and therefore needs an owner-confirmed boundary.

options.title: Enforce on every browser-origin request
options.body: Apply the shared origin check whenever Origin or browser fetch metadata is present, while leaving requests without browser headers available to trusted host automation.

options.title: Limit enforcement to identity-bearing auth
options.body: Keep token/password protected by bearer authentication and enforce origin only for trusted-proxy requests, documenting auth.mode="none" as fully ingress-owned.

options.title: Require per-route anti-CSRF tokens
options.body: Add a separate nonce contract to mutable plugin HTTP routes, increasing client and compatibility cost beyond the existing origin and bearer model.

recommendation.title: Enforce on every browser-origin request
recommendation.body: Apply the shared origin check whenever Origin or browser fetch metadata is present, while leaving requests without browser headers available to trusted host automation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history spans the ACP and Gateway/plugin control-plane boundaries needed to confirm the intended product-wide HTTP security policy.
